chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
title: Leo Williams, the tenor player who matched Charlie Parker
summary: Williams, who toured Chicago with Trummy's band, became Parker's close friend and was called his equal.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Anyway, I don't remember whether I mentioned the fact that when we went to Chicago with Trummy, that the tenor saxophone player was a guy whose name was Leo Williams. I don't know whether I mentioned his name. I know I mentioned Tommy Potter and Harry Curtis, the alto saxophone player, Trummy, of course, and Eddie Bert. I don't know if I did mention him or not, but Leo Williams was one of those
exceptionally good musicians, and an exceptionally talented musician.

As a matter of fact, later, when Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie heard him, they just loved him. He and Charlie Parker became very fast friends. And it was always said that you listen to Leo and you listen to Charlie Parker, it was 50-50, you know. Leo played tenor saxophone. But Leo was the kind of guy that he did everything Charlie Parker did, and they were like two peas in a pod for a long while.
